verdict.rationale: cubic's docs show reviews use repository context beyond the diff. They detect and use context files such as README.md, AGENTS.md and .cursorrules, learn team conventions from feedback and historical reviews, and can link related repositories to check shared APIs and schemas. However, no doc states that PR review comments analyze call sites or related modules within the same repository; the 'reads the rest of your codebase' claim applies to the separate AI chat sidebar, not review comments. Missing for 10: explicit documentation that PR reviews trace in-repo call sites and dependent modules, and independent or hands-on corroboration of whole-repo-aware review comments.

support.subject: As a developer, review comments reflect the whole repository — call sites, related modules, existing conventions — not just the changed hunks

citations.quote: cubic automatically detects and uses context files in your repository, including `README.md`, `context.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `.cursorrules`, agent skills directories, and files in `.ai/` directories.
Link related repositories so reviews can check shared APIs, schemas, docs, or release work.
cubic learns your team's unwritten rules from two sources: direct feedback on its comments, and patterns extracted from your senior engineers' historical code reviews.
